The Supreme Court opens a new term this week.
NPR's Nina Totenberg takes a look at some of the cases that could come before the court.
Even as the justices will hear major cases on climate change, immigration, guns and religion,
there are many more hot-button issues waiting in the wings.
Among them, whether the court will reverse nearly a half-century-old precedent
that bars the posting of the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms.
More immediately, though, the justices are likely to be drawn into the election.
The Trump administration has sought to influence elections in numerous ways,
and Democrats have lawyers across the country ready to fight what they perceive as illegal measures.
In the end, though, some of these clashes are bound to make it to the Supreme Court.
Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
Authorities in Japan have arrested a U.S. Marine in connection with the alleged murder of a woman on the island of Okinawa.
NPR's Scott Newman has the story.
Prefectural police arrested the 20-year-old Marine assigned to Okinawa's Fatemna Air Station.
According to Japan's Kyoto News Service,
authorities believe the Marine robbed and strangled a 39-year-old local woman at a hotel in the capital, Naha.
Okinawa's governor called the incident "absolutely unforgivable" and said Okinawans are "outraged."
About half of the 50,000 U.S. troops stationed in Japan are in Okinawa.
Their presence has been a source of friction for years,
with a number of high-profile murders and sexual assaults involving American service members.
Scott Newman, NPR News.
Allegations of a gang rape at a Cornell University fraternity house are reigniting a national reckoning.
The nation's biggest anti-sexual assault hotline says calls have spiked since the case emerged.
NPR's Amy Held reports.
This unfortunately feels all too familiar for many, many people.
Megan Cutter is chief of victim services at RAIN.
Someone in the United States is sexually assaulted every 68 seconds.
But they may not think of it that way at first.
A survivor's perception of their own experience, it is really common for that to change over time.
The "I Am Jane Doe" campaign is letting people express solidarity.
Shay Thomas is a student at Cornell.
This is a movement that is meant to help bring light to the issues of women who have to deal with sexual harassment or assault.
Aisha Matan is a postdoc researcher at Cornell.
Every time I scroll through, it's just people talking about their similar incident.
Even, she says, from 30 years ago.
Amy Held, NPR News.
Polls have closed in Brazil in a pivotal presidential election featuring incumbent Luis Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.
A runoff election will be held October 25th if neither candidate manages to secure a majority.
You're listening to NPR News.
A large gray shark has captivated the attention of people in South Korea.
Authorities are trying to free the animal from a canal, or it's been stuck for more than two weeks.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul.
The 11-and-a-half-foot-long gray shark has been named Bukangi after the North Port Park in the port city of Busan, where he's stuck.
Authorities have used jets of water and nets to try to coax Bukangi back out to sea, but the shark has so far ignored or dodged them all.
Over half a million people have come to see him.
He's gone viral on social media, and last week the city officially appointed him as an honorary ambassador.
While tourists are entertained by Bukangi, there is concern about his health if he remains trapped in the canal.
And environmental activists and marine biologists say Bukangi's presence may be a warning sign that warming seas are driving marine life north.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
The satire "Digger" has flopped in its opening weekend at the box office, grossing a mere $8 million nationwide
and handing Tom Cruise one of the worst debuts of his career.
The poor showing for "Digger" comes as Warner Bros. is poised to merge with Paramount.
This would end Warner Bros. history as a stand-alone movie studio.
The number one movie in North American theaters this weekend was "Verity."
It brought in $32.6 million at the box offices in its opening weekend.
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
